facts.title: Visa-free for up to 45 days (tourism)
facts.body: Tourism only, up to 45 days (policy 15 Aug 2025 – 14 Aug 2028). You need a return or onward ticket and documents showing the purpose of your trip. Longer or other purposes: e-visa (up to 90 days) only via evisa.gov.vn.

sources.title: New visa exemption policies — Vietnam National Authority of Tourism

facts.title: Passport ≥6 months on arrival
facts.body: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival.

facts.title: Don't overstay
facts.body: An expired visa can mean a fine or prison. An extension is only possible before it expires — contact the immigration department in time.

facts.title: Digital pre-arrival form
facts.body: Mandatory when landing at Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Da Nang or Phu Quoc airports; optional elsewhere.

facts.title: Land borders not always open
facts.body: Border areas with neighbouring countries are not always open. Ask the local authorities (e.g. the police) about the current situation.

facts.title: Pickpockets
facts.body: Especially in busy city and tourist areas; avoid remote streets and parks.

facts.title: Landmines and UXO
facts.body: Quang Tri province, central Vietnam and along the Laos border. Stay on main roads and marked paths, hike only with someone who knows the area, and never touch metal objects.

facts.title: Traffic accidents
facts.body: Many deaths and injuries every year, mostly on mopeds and scooters, tourists included. Consider a car with driver. If you ride: under 50 cc only, only with experience, and with insurance that covers vehicle accidents.

facts.title: Typhoons May–November; northern landslides
facts.body: Tropical storms mainly May–November. After heavy rain, landslides and mudflows in the northern mountains (Dien Bien, Sapa, Ha Giang) can close roads.

facts.title: Limited healthcare; malaria, rabies, air pollution
facts.body: Serious cases may need transfer abroad. The GGD covers malaria and rabies; air pollution can cause respiratory problems.

facts.title: Drugs: death penalty possible; bar drug tests
facts.body: Soft drugs included. Police drug-test people in bars and clubs; a positive result from use weeks ago or abroad can still lead to arrest.

facts.title: Vapes banned
facts.body: Bringing, using or selling e-cigarettes and refills: high fine or 1–15 years in prison.

facts.title: No photos of military or police
facts.body: Photographing military sites, soldiers, police or guards is forbidden and can lead to arrest.

facts.title: Grab
facts.body: Grab (rides and food) operates in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hoi An, Hue, Ninh Binh, Phu Quoc and many other cities.

facts.title: Driving needs an IDP
facts.body: A Dutch licence is only valid with an IDP. Scooters: under 50 cc only.

facts.title: Plugs: A, C, D; 220 V
facts.body: Mains is 220 V / 50 Hz; sockets usually take A and C plugs (often universal), sometimes D. A universal adapter covers it.

facts.title: Tết 2027: around 6 February
facts.body: Lunar New Year falls on 6 Feb 2027. The official public holiday was not final at the time of writing (proposed 4–10 Feb). Expect full trains, buses and flights and many closed shops and restaurants for about a week around it.

sources.title: Vietnam ministry backs 7-day Lunar New Year break in 2027 — Tuoi Tre
